consultant friend:

"the reason you see people jump to consulting later in their career is that being able to see the anti-patterns makes it too painful to be on the inside, but they genuinely still want to help humans"

amazing how "stop starting, start finishing" is *so much more effective* than "reduce work in progress".

and they are basically equivalent.

if you're going to run a messy cross-team, cross-functional, cross-department project

run. the. project

get everyone in a "room" daily. cross your Ts. Dot Is. full attention. checklists. regular retros (with everyone)

there's nothing worse than a middling big project

product manager / designer superpower...

 letting people rattle on about their solutions as a way to unearth their assumptions/beliefs, and then "letting them down easy" while doing something all-together different with those beliefs as inputs

aka...ideas are data
Some insanely high % of product management is trying to make sure team members  interpret fifteen words in roughly the same way.

I had a epiphany the other day...

by going through the motions and doing your best in your current company (even if your company isn't ready for what you have in mind)

...even if things "don't work", you'll set yourself up well for your next job

there's a benefit in practice
